what_its_for: Clemastine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and itchy throat or skin. It can also help with hives (urticaria) and other allergic skin reactions.
how_to_take: Take clemastine by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or a full glass of water. Swallow tablets whole. Do not crush or chew extended-release forms unless your pharmacist tells you it is safe to do so. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older: the usual dose is 1.34 mg (1 tablet) taken twice a day, or 2.68 mg taken once or twice daily for hives, depending on the product. Do not take more than 8.04 mg in 24 hours. For children under 12, follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Always use the lowest dose that controls your symptoms.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store clemastine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking clemastine, as it can greatly increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do any activity that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medications that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, muscle relaxants, anxiety medicines, or other antihistamines, unless your doctor approves. Avoid taking with MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine or selegiline).
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or seek medical help right away if you experience: severe drowsiness or confusion, difficulty urinating or no urination, fast or irregular heartbeat, vision changes or eye pain, seizures, signs of an allergic reaction (rash, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing), or if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of use.
when_it_works: Clemastine usually starts working within 1 to 2 hours after you take it. The effects can last 10 to 12 hours. You may notice relief from sneezing, runny nose, and itching fairly quickly after your first dose.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): Use with extra caution. Clemastine can cause more severe drowsiness, dizziness, confusion, and difficulty urinating in older people, increasing the risk of falls. A lower dose may be recommended. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it may not be recommended. Children under 12: Only use under a doctor's guidance. Kidney or liver problems: Let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver disease, as dose adjustments may be needed. Enlarged prostate, glaucoma, or asthma: Tell your doctor about these conditions before starting clemastine.
